cases.name: an initial entry that spawns four promises runs once, through the start and each promise's done
cases.test: actor.test.ts > actors > should only spawn actors defined on initial state once (the counter is the context's count, incremented by the entry that spawns; each spawn is a spawnChild of a host actor under an id of its own, the references array having no JSON form)

cases.name: a child invoked in the parent's initial state spawns its promise once when the parent starts
cases.test: actor.test.ts > actors > should spawn an actor in an initial state of a child that gets invoked in the initial state of a parent when the parent gets started (the spawn counter is the one pending request of the child's promise)

cases.name: a machine spawned on start that pings its parent from its entry takes the parent to done
cases.test: actor.test.ts > actors > should only spawn an initial actor once when it synchronously responds with an event (the context factory's spawn is a spawnChild in the root's entry, which runs in the same initial macrostep; the factory's call counter is the context's count, incremented by that entry)

cases.name: a promise spawned by the root's entry fulfills with 42 and its done event completes the parent
cases.test: actor.test.ts > actors > with actor logic > should work with a promise logic (fulfill) (the guard event.output === 42 is event_equals on output)

cases.name: a promise spawned on start rejects and its error event completes the parent
cases.test: actor.test.ts > actors > with actor logic > should work with a promise logic (reject) (the context factory's spawn is a spawnChild in the root's entry; the guard event.error === errorMessage is event_equals on error)

cases.name: a machine spawned on start sends TEST to its parent from its entry and the parent completes
cases.test: actor.test.ts > actors > should be able to spawn machines in (lazy) initial context (the context factory's spawn is a spawnChild in the root's entry, which runs in the same initial macrostep)

cases.name: a child spawned by the root's entry that is done at once leaves its parent active
cases.test: actor.test.ts > actors > should not crash on child machine sync completion during self-initialization (not throwing is the root's status active)

cases.name: a promise spawned on an event rejects and its unhandled error fails the parent with that error
cases.test: actor.test.ts > actors > catches errors from spawned promise actors (the thrown Error('uh oh') is the rejection {message: 'uh oh'}; the error observer's argument is the root's status error and its snapshot's error)

cases.name: a promise spawned by the root's entry that settles with null right after start leaves its parent active
cases.test: actor.test.ts > actors > should not crash on child promise-like sync completion during self-initialization (not throwing is the root's status active, after the start and after the child's done event; the thenable that calls back at once settles in a microtask after start returns, as fromPromise wraps it in Promise.resolve, which is the resolve step with null that follows the start; a spawnChild with the id child stands for the spawn inside the entry's assign, whose child XState keys by its session id (x:1); the reference assign keeps in the context, an actor reference as data, is not ported)

excluded.test: actor.test.ts > actors > same-position invokes should not leak between machines
excluded.reason: the test's subject is a leak between two machines created with one shared implementations object, each invoking an inline fromPromise at the same position (0.(machine)); a case has no inline src, by the divergence "An invoke's src" (every src names an actor of the case's own "actors"), each machine declares its own actors, and a case creates one root, so no second machine can share or overwrite what the first resolves. What would remain, an onDone receiving its promise's output 'foo' once, is an ordinary invoke and not the leak.
